articles.title: Marnus Labuschagne named in Australia squad to face South Africa
articles.summary: Out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne is named in the Australia squad for next month's three-Test tour of South Africa.
articles.body:
Out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne has been named in the Australia squad for next month's three-Test tour of South Africa.

Number three Labuschagne, 32, who was born in South Africa, has failed to score a century since 2023 and struggled in two Tests against Bangladesh last month.

Having scored one, 31 and four, he was then left out of Australia's squad for three one-day internationals in Zimbabwe and another three in South Africa.

"[We're] not shying away from the fact that we'd like some more runs from Marn... but we're also confident that he can still make a positive contribution to that squad," chief Australia selector George Bailey said.

"Our batting group in its entirety, not just Marn, probably hasn't been functioning as successfully as we would like."

Asked if the South Africa series would be Labuschagne's last chance, Bailey replied: "No, I wouldn't say that. But again, it's a hypothetical, isn't it?"

It will be Australia's first Test series in South Africa since the infamous 'Sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal in 2018.

Captain Steve Smith and vice-skipper David Warner were banned for a year for using sandpaper to damage the ball during the third Test.

Only captain Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon, Smith and Matt Renshaw survive from the 3-1 series defeat in 2018.

Cooper Connolly, Matthew Kuhnemann and Michael Neser were also included in the 16-man squad, which is otherwise unchanged from the last Bangladesh Test.

Australia travel to Durban for the first Test on 9 October before the series moves to Gqeberha and Cape Town.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen joins England white-ball set-up as specialist mentor
articles.summary: England appoint former Ashes-winning batter Kevin Pietersen to their white-ball coaching team in the build-up to the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.
articles.body:
England have appointed former Ashes-winning batter Kevin Pietersen to their white-ball coaching team in the build-up to the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.

Pietersen, 46, joins as a specialist mentor and will start in the role for the upcoming T20 and one-day matches against Sri Lanka.

He will also be involved in this winter's tours to Australia and South Africa, before joining up with the teams again for the home series against Pakistan and New Zealand next summer, as well as the 50-over World Cup, which is being held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in the autumn.

"I've got immense respect for KP and what he's achieved in the game," said England's white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum.

"He's had an amazing impact on English cricket, so for someone with his experience, knowledge and stature to want to play a role with this team is a fantastic result."

Pietersen is one of England's most successful white-ball batters, being named player of the tournament when they won the T20 World Cup for the first time in 2010.

The right-hander scored almost 4,500 ODI runs at an average of 41.32 - bettered only by Joe Root - while in T20 cricket he has the highest average of all batters to hit more than 1,000 runs for England.

He did, however, fall out with a number of former England players and coaches during his career.

He was accused of being "divisive" in the dressing room and was dropped during a Test series against South Africa in 2012 for sending "provocative" text messages to opposing players, for which he apologised to then captain Andrew Strauss.

He was only allowed to return to the team after a successful 'reintegration' period.

Pietersen was also one of the first to advocate for England players being allowed to play in the Indian Premier League and other white-ball franchise leagues around the world - a stance which often put him at odds with his employers.

Since retiring, Pietersen has enjoyed a successful career as a commentator and content creator while he has mentored in the Indian Premier League for Delhi Capitals.

"I am immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa," said Pietersen.

"Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment.

"We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad, and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential."

Pietersen spoke about his coaching ambitions earlier in 2026, , external after England's 4-1 Ashes hammering in Australia.

Though this role is with the white-ball teams, he said he would "love" to help coach the Test side, telling the Guardian he has "got all the credentials" and has "worn every ​single T-shirt".

Hinting at his approach, he added: "In the shortest ‌form ⁠of the game, sure, play without fear, go out there, be brave, be reckless, be careless, be whatever you want. In Test match cricket, you cannot do that."

He also criticised England's coaching set-up, led by McCullum, during a white-ball tour to India in 2025.

"I'm sorry, but I am absolutely gobsmacked that England did not have one team practice session since losing the first ODI and losing the T20 series," said Pietersen, who was working as a commentator for the host broadcaster.

Pietersen's first assignment will be a three-match T20 series against Sri Lanka, which begins on 15 September in Southampton.

This is quite a return to international cricket for a man who was effectively fired by England 12 years ago.

After all the animosity and acrimony that followed the end of Kevin Pietersen's playing career at the very highest level, he is back with the Three Lions on his chest.

For England, this is the first step in reshaping the backroom teams in the new era of split coaches. It is also not the first time they have hired a big name to act as a consultant to the white-ball side, following Andrew Flintoff and Kieron Pollard.

In terms of intrigue, the appointment of Pietersen outstrips anything that has come before.

Perhaps the greatest white-ball batter to play for England, his knowledge and experience will bring an X-factor to the coaching staff.

It's also a smart move given his expertise of playing in South Africa, the venue of the next 50-over World Cup. Who could forget Pietersen announcing himself as an international cricketer in the country of his birth in 2005, smashing runs against the Proteas in a one-day series?

What could Pietersen bring to the game of Harry Brook, for example? Brook is the closest England have produced to another Pietersen, yet has admitted he still needs to make better decisions in the middle. It was a criticism Pietersen often faced during his career.

Along with Brook, the England dressing room is filled with players who grew up watching and idolising Pietersen. There should be a queue of batters wanting to work with him.

But there will also be a nagging doubt over whether this could go wrong at any moment. Pietersen is not shy of speaking his mind, or clashing with authority. He joins a dressing room run by Brendon McCullum, another big personality.

Either way, it promises to be box-office stuff.

articles.title: 'Nothing is taken for granted': Devdutt Padikkal on cementing his place in Test team
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India's top-order batter Devdutt Padikkal knows that consistent performances are the key to keeping his place in the Test team. Padikkal sa.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's top-order batter Devdutt Padikkal knows that consistent performances are the key to keeping his place in the Test team. Padikkal said he wants to keep scoring runs and contribute to India's wins. He believes that if he continues to perform, his place in the team will take care of itself.The left-hander enjoyed an excellent tour of Sri Lanka, scoring back-to-back centuries as India won the two-match series 1-0. He was also named Player of the Series.Batting at No. 3 in the absence of Sai Sudharsan, Padikkal impressed with his solid technique and ability to score quickly.'I was really looking forward to it'Padikkal said he was excited when he learned that he would play in the series. He also felt he was batting at the best stage of his career."Definitely, I was looking forward to it. Obviously, those opportunities don't come very easily. It takes a lot of hard work to make sure that you are continuing to improve yourself and waiting for that opportunity. I had to make sure that I was ready whenever I got it.“The fact that I was told at the start of the series that I was going to be playing was really exciting, and I felt like, personally, I was at the best stage of my career in terms of the way I was batting, so I was really looking forward to it," Padikkal told JioStar.No pressure over No. 3 comparisonsPadikkal has taken over the important No. 3 position, a spot previously occupied by India greats such as Rahul Dravid and Cheteshwar Pujara.However, the batter said he does not want to worry about comparisons with the legends who played the position before him."At the end of the day, it's about going out there and batting. It doesn't matter what position I'm batting at, I'm trying to contribute to the side.“Yes, obviously, there have been great players who have played at number three for India over the years, and I'm sure there'll be a lot more scrutiny on me and a lot more comparisons made. But at the end of the day, I'm going out there and just playing my cricket, and as long as I'm enjoying that, I think everything will fall into place," he said.Dravid's advice helped PadikkalPadikkal also spoke about his conversations with former India head coach Rahul Dravid. He said Dravid helped him understand what it takes to bat for long periods in Test cricket."Obviously, I've had a lot of conversations with him over the years in terms of batting and what it takes to really spend long hours out there.“Again, it comes back to preparation and understanding what you want to do. As long as you have that clarity in your head about what your plans are and what you want to go out there and do, regardless of the position you're batting at, it helps a lot. I think those are the conversations I've had with him."‘Nothing is taken for granted’With India set for a busy Test schedule, including a tour of New Zealand and a five-match Border-Gavaskar Trophy series against Australia early next year, Padikkal knows that he cannot take his place for granted.He said scoring runs regularly and helping India win matches will remain his main focus."As long as I'm scoring runs, I think it always benefits the side. Test cricket is not the easiest format, as we all know, so you have to keep performing day in and day out. You get limited opportunities these days, and it's not very easy to cement a place in a side.“Nothing is taken for granted. For me, personally, I just want to keep scoring runs and keep contributing to wins for the Indian Test side. As long as I'm doing that, I'm sure I'll have my place."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen: England appoint former captain as specialist mentor for white-ball teams
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen will form part of England's coaching setup at the 2027 Cricket World Cup in October and November next year; the former Ashes and T20 World Cup winner said: "Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment"
articles.body:
Pietersen will join head coach Brendon McCullum's white-ball setup for the T20 international and ODI series' against Sri Lanka later this month, part of a coaching team that also includes Marcus Trescothick, Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor.

The former England captain said of his appointment: "I'm immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa.

"Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment.

"We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad, and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential.

"To be a part of Brendon's think tank over the next 12 months is a fantastic opportunity, and I cannot wait to get started."

McCullum said: "I've got immense respect for KP and what he's achieved in the game. He's had an amazing impact on English cricket, so for someone with his experience, knowledge and stature to want to play a role with this team is a fantastic result.

"I'm particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him. KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players. We've always respected each other and had a strong appreciation for what the other brings to the game, so I'm really looking forward to working together."

Pietersen will be involved in England's winter's white-ball tours to Australia and South Africa, before joining up with the teams again for the home series against Pakistan and New Zealand next summer, as well as the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

The former Ashes and T20 World Cup winner played 136 ODIs and 37 T20 matches for England, scoring more than 5,500 runs, adding another 8,181 runs across his 104 Test match appearances.

Pietersen has previously worked as a mentor for Delhi Capitals during the 2025 Indian Premier League.

articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana has been fined 10 per cent of her match fee and given one demerit point for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct during the .
articles.body: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana has been fined 10 per cent of her match fee and given one demerit point for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct during the Women's Asia Cup match against India.Pakistan lost the Group A match by seven wickets at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday.The International Cricket Council (ICC) said on Monday that Fatima had breached Article 2.5 of the Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel.The rule relates to ‘using language, actions or gestures which disparage, or which could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon his/her dismissal during an International Match.’Gesture after dismissing ShafaliThe incident took place on the final ball of the second over of India's chase of 56.Fatima dismissed India opener Shafali Verma through a caught-and-bowled dismissal. After taking the catch, the Pakistan captain gestured towards the pavilion.The gesture led to the Code of Conduct charge.Second offence in 24 monthsThis is Fatima's second offence within a 24-month period. Her latest demerit point takes her total to two.Her previous demerit point came during Pakistan's opening T20 International against Ireland in Dublin on August 6, 2025."Fatima admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by Supriya Rani Das of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees, so there was no need for a formal hearing," further said the ICC.The charges were brought by on-field umpires Nimali Perera and Shathira Jakir Jesy, third umpire Rokeya Sultana and fourth umpire Rabab Ahsan.Level 1 breaches carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand and a maximum penalty of 50 per cent of a player's match fee. Players can also receive one or two demerit points.Fatima available for Hong Kong matchDespite the penalty, Fatima will be available to lead Pakistan in their next Women's Asia Cup match against Hong Kong China on Tuesday.Pakistan need a win to reach the semi-finals.Seven-time champions India and defending champions Sri Lanka have already secured their places in the last four.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner is expecting a tough challenge when India’s ODI specialists Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma return to New Zealand la.
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner is expecting a tough challenge when India’s ODI specialists Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma return to New Zealand later this year. Kohli and Rohit now play only ODI cricket and will be back in action when India tour New Zealand for five ODIs, five T20Is and two Tests in October-November.Santner knows the experienced Indian batters have enjoyed playing in New Zealand in the past. He hopes that will not be the case this time."It is going to be a challenge. They are still very good players as we have seen for a long time; masters of the ODI game. They have taken a liking to some New Zealand pitches in the past. Hopefully, not this time around," Santner told PTI."It is going to be a great series, no doubt. It is all a lead-up for the World Cup next year in ODIs. Everyone is trying to figure out their best team; what that might look like for October next year with limited games."New Zealand want to beat India at homeSantner said New Zealand's first target will be to win the ODI series against India at home.The Blackcaps will play five ODIs against India, followed by three ODIs against Sri Lanka at home. They will then travel to England for World Cup preparations in September 2027."We've got five (matches) against India, three against Sri Lanka at home and then it is World Cup prep in England (in September 2027), right before the World Cup," he said."(But) first things first, you want to win a series against India at home, which would be an awesome thing. Then it is (about) trying to find what the make-up might look like come October next year," Santner added.India tour of New Zealand: Full scheduleDateMatchVenueTime (IST)Oct 22, 20261st T20IHagley Oval, Christchurch12:30 PMOct 24, 20262nd T20IHagley Oval, Christchurch12:30 PMOct 27, 20263rd T20ISky Stadium, Wellington12:30 PMOct 30, 20264th T20IEden Park, Auckland12:30 PMNov 1, 20265th T20ISeddon Park, Hamilton12:30 PMNov 4, 20261st ODIEden Park, Auckland7:30 AMNov 7, 20262nd ODISky Stadium, Wellington7:30 AMNov 10, 20263rd ODISeddon Park, Hamilton7:30 AMNov 13, 20264th ODIBay Oval, Mount Maunganui7:30 AMNov 15, 20265th ODIBay Oval, Mount Maunganui7:30 AMNov 19–23, 20261st TestBasin Reserve, Wellington3:30 AMNov 27–Dec 1, 20262nd TestHagley Oval, Christchurch3:30 AMSantner recalls India's 3-0 Test lossIndia and New Zealand last met in a Test series in India, with the Kiwis recording a historic 3-0 win. The result ended India's unbeaten home Test run, which had lasted more than 12 years and 18 series.With India's Test team now going through a change, Santner believes the two-Test series in New Zealand could be difficult for some of the new players."I think what we spoke about before is trying to adapt quickly," said Santner, who took 7/53 and 6/104 in the second Test at Pune to seal the series win, recalling the tour."For a new-look India side, it is probably going to be the first time some players have been playing red-ball (cricket) in New Zealand, where the pitches will be a little bit foreign. They will probably do a bit more than they might do back home."‘Very well-rounded’ India squadSantner, however, feels India's current Test team is strong and has a good balance.He described the squad as "well-rounded" and said it has been "shaping up nicely"."If you look at their squad, it is a very well-rounded squad. You throw (Jasprit) Bumrah back into the bowling attack, you have got (Mohammed) Siraj, (Prasidh) Krishna with the bounce. You have got (Ravindra) Jadeja and (Manav) Suthar to bowl spin. You have got probably a fourth seamer in there as well.""It is shaping up nicely. I think it is going to be a great series. Traditionally, it can do a little bit in New Zealand at that time of the year," Santner said.‘Fight fire with fire’Santner also spoke about how teams may need to approach Test cricket in New Zealand. He said batters may have to play their shots at times, while also being ready to defend and see off the new ball.He continued, "It could be trying to fight fire with fire, playing your shots. There might be times we need to sit back and let the bowlers go for a bit, try to get the shine off the ball. There is a lot that can go on in the Test matches in New Zealand. It is going to be an exciting series and one that we can't wait for."Why only two Tests?When asked why the India-New Zealand series has only two Tests, Santner pointed to New Zealand's history of playing shorter Test series as well as financial factors."For a long time, New Zealand played two-match series. There’s obviously the money side of it as well.""I know it costs a lot to play Test cricket. (It is about) timing as well; white-ball brings in the crowds in New Zealand, it brings the money. That's why I guess it is the 10-2 split."However, Santner said playing India, even in a two-Test series, remains a major opportunity for New Zealand."Whenever India come, even if it is only two Test matches, it is going to be exciting. Everyone wants to challenge themselves against the best in the world and they are up there. For us, it is going to be an important series like it is for India with the (World Test Championship) points that are on offer."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ishan Kishan's 270 lights up Duleep Trophy final; East Zone pile up 708 vs South Zone
articles.summary: Cricket News: Ishan Kishan produced a superb batting performance in difficult humid conditions as East Zone posted a huge 708 against South Zone on the second day o.
articles.body: Ishan Kishan produced a superb batting performance in difficult humid conditions as East Zone posted a huge 708 against South Zone on the second day of the Duleep Trophy final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai on Monday. Kishan scored a massive 270, once again showing the selectors his ability in red-ball cricket. Three national selectors were present to watch his innings.He batted for 522 minutes and faced 334 balls over nearly two days. His innings was the biggest highlight of a dominant East Zone batting display.Kushagra provides strong supportKumar Kushagra also played an important role, scoring his sixth first-class century.The 21-year-old made 101 off 132 balls, with eight fours and five sixes. He attacked the South Zone bowlers with shots on both sides of the wicket.However, he could not stay till the end. His casual pull against a short delivery from Tripurana Vijay ended in the hands of CV Milind at square leg.Kishan misses out on triple centuryKishan came close to joining the small group of batters who have scored triple centuries in the Duleep Trophy.Raman Lamba and Gagan Khoda are the only batters to have achieved the feat, in 1987 and 2001 respectively.Kishan eventually fell on 270, but his innings remained one of the most impressive knocks of the tournament.There was a touch of Virender Sehwag in his batting — he attacked with confidence, scored quickly when needed and made full use of the conditions.A slower second hundredKishan reached his first century on Sunday in just 122 balls.His second hundred took longer, with the next 100 runs coming off 148 balls. The slowdown was not because of a difficult pitch or a special spell from the South Zone bowlers.Instead, Kishan appeared to be taking fewer risks, focusing on tiring out the bowlers and helping East Zone build a huge total.He completed his second first-class double century in 270 balls, hitting part-time spinner Devdutt Padikkal through the covers for a boundary.Kishan attacks the spinnersAfter reaching 200, Kishan shifted gears again.He scored the next 50 runs in just 31 balls, taking on Shreyas Gopal and Tripurana Vijay.Both spinners were hit for two sixes each. Kishan scored 94 runs off 100 balls against Shreyas, while Vijay conceded 70 runs from 88 balls.Pulls and drives remained Kishan's main scoring shots. He hit 22 fours through those strokes.South Zone bowlers struggleSouth Zone's bowlers had very little impact for the second day in a row.Mohammed Siraj, their main fast bowler, could not trouble the East Zone batters as the flat pitch and high-quality batting made life difficult for the bowling attack.Kishan also had one uncomfortable moment when left-arm pacer CV Milind hit him on the abdomen. He received quick medical attention and continued batting.Kishan walks off after 250After a marathon innings, fatigue finally caught up with Kishan.He walked off the field retired hurt after scoring 250 off 301 balls, with 27 fours and seven sixes.His innings had already done most of the damage.East Zone added 106 runs in the first session and another 135 after lunch. Kishan also shared a 230-run partnership with Kushagra for the fifth wicket in just 290 balls.He then added 140 with Anukul Roy, who scored 40 off 86 balls, for the sixth wicket.Kishan falls short of 300Kishan returned to the middle after Mohammad Shami was dismissed early in the final session.With East Zone already in a dominant position, he had a chance to become only the third batter to score a triple century in the Duleep Trophy.But the landmark remained out of reach.Kishan hit Vijay, who finished with figures of 4/180, straight into the hands of Ravichandran Smaran near the sight screen.By then, however, Kishan had already done more than enough to put East Zone in a commanding position.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan investigate 'discipline and conduct' on turbulent tour
articles.summary: Pakistan begin an inquiry into “discipline and conduct” in the latest twist on a turbulent tour of England.
articles.body:
Pakistan have begun an inquiry into "discipline and conduct" in the latest twist on a turbulent tour of England.

Already 2-0 down in the three-match Test series, Pakistan last week sent seven players home, called up seven more and replaced head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with New Zealander Mike Hesson.

During the second Test at Lord's, the tourists also threatened to cancel the remainder of the match and the tour over an interview broadcast by Sky with the sons of imprisoned former Pakistan prime minister and captain Imran Khan.

In a statement released on Monday morning, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) said: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.

"The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration."

The statement refers to "speculative reports" from "hostile external sources".

Last week, Hesson responded to reports Salman Ali Agha - one of the seven dropped players - refused to attend a meeting with King Charles at Clarence House.

Hesson also refuted suggestions that Mohammad Imran and Mohammad Imran Jr were both called up as replacements because the PCB was confused by their names.

The statement continued: "At this stage, any speculative reports or unverified claims circulating on certain platforms, particularly those originating from hostile external sources, should not be regarded as credible.

"The PCB will not comment further at this time. The Board advises stakeholders and the public to rely on official PCB communications."

Pakistan players used to 'chaos' - head coach Hesson

Last week, Hesson did explain how Pakistan came to omit seven players from their original touring party.

Four changes were made to the bowling attack after Hesson was asked to take charge for the final Test.

However, three experienced players were dropped before Hesson came in. They were Salman, fellow batter Imam-ul-Haq and wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan.

Imam came in for criticism during the second Test at Lord's for not batting in either innings because of a calf injury.

Along with Hesson coming in as head coach, Australian Ashley Noffke has been added to the backroom staff as a replacement for fast-bowling coach Umar Gul.

Speaking on Monday at Edgbaston in the build-up to Wednesday's final Test, Noffke said he was not aware of any details of the investigation.

"I don't know too much. I sit outside that decision-making model, above us as coaches," he said.

"I guess that's one thing I've learned about being in Pakistan and coaching for a period of time, nearly 15 months with the white-ball team - there's always something going on in the background.

"Whether or not it's in or out of our control – and most of the time it's out of the players' control. We're not really in the position to know the outer workings of what's happening at the PCB in that context."

articles.title: 'Not overthinking, not keeping expectations': Ishan Kishan reveals mindset behind epic 270 in Duleep Trophy final
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan believes having a clear mind has helped him rediscover his best form. After hitting a stunning 270 in the Duleep Trophy final,.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan believes having a clear mind has helped him rediscover his best form. After hitting a stunning 270 in the Duleep Trophy final, East Zone captain Kishan said he has learned to avoid overthinking and putting unnecessary pressure on himself.For Kishan, the focus is now simple - score runs and help his team win matches. His marathon knock against South Zone was a clear sign of the change in his mindset after a difficult phase in his career."I didn't actively try to change myself. It just happened naturally. When I was out of the (India) squad, I realised that we ultimately only have one job to do: simply to score runs. That is the only thing that helps you in your career," Kishan said in the post-day press meet."Any other thoughts will only manipulate your mindset, push you into overthinking, and pile on unnecessary pressure. I realised that those extraneous thoughts aren't necessary. Our job is to step in and win matches for the team. That's all you should care about. You evolve with time, and I feel it is much easier to play this way when you keep your mind clear," he added.From India regular to domestic cricketKishan was an all-format India player in 2023, but a series of events saw him lose his place in the team and eventually his BCCI central contract. He then returned to domestic cricket and worked hard to rebuild his career.Kishan scored centuries in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy and played an important role in Jharkhand's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy triumph. He scored 517 runs in the tournament, including two hundreds. His strong performances soon earned him a BCCI contract and a return to India's white-ball teams.‘My job as a batsman is just to go there’Kishan said he now tries not to think too much about the result or his position in the team."The best thing I'm doing nowadays is not thinking about anything. My job as a batsman is just to go there, watch the ball, and react to it and not keep any expectations from myself. At times, you will, obviously, lose patience. But that is the time when you have to talk to yourself; you have to control that, calm your thoughts about whether you are taking the right decision or not, and after that, you execute your plans,” he said.Preparing for red-ball cricketKishan also explained how he prepared for the Duleep Trophy after spending time playing white-ball cricket.“I was here at the BCCI CoE before coming here. We were practicing there, specifically with the red ball. When you play T20s regularly, you start playing a lot of shots — which is what happened in my first innings against the North East Zone (in Duleep Trophy). In the middle, I went to play a cut and then got double-minded about whether to hit it or not and got out.”Ahead of the final, Kishan changed his focus and spent more time building partnerships instead of looking for quick runs.Building partnerships was the key“When you're playing a final and you are already a multi-format player, who has played for India for quite some time, the team members expect you to score runs. So, it's very important for me to be in the middle and get as many runs for your team.“The plan remained simple: keep adding 50-run partnerships as much as possible. A lot of things factor in picking up when their bowlers are tiring, when they are opening up the field—so you keep batting around these things without worrying about the result,” he explained.Kishan reflects on his domestic stintKishan said returning to domestic cricket was not something he considered a punishment.Instead, he enjoyed the experience and used the time to reflect on his game and understand where he needed to improve."I genuinely enjoyed it because I went back, had to grind and work hard for about two years (when he was out of the team). But sometimes, what happens is, when we play regularly for the Indian team, you just keep playing in a flow. You might be a very good player which is why you're playing for India, but your growth stagnates at a certain point. So when you take one step back and go back to domestic cricket, you start from zero again."You start thinking, 'I need to get even better,' because today, there are so many players scoring runs. So, to get back into the team, your only option is to perform much better than them.“Nothing against anyone, but I'm saying you'll only benefit if you do better. So, you have to start again. You get time to reflect on what you missed earlier, why you couldn't convert your starts into big scores. The batting doesn't change that much; it's just the mindset that changes over time," he detailed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'North pole and south pole': Ashish Nehra compares Shubman Gill and Hardik Pandya as captains
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill is still learning the art of captaincy and will improve with experience, Gujarat Titans head coach Ashish Nehra said on Monday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill is still learning the art of captaincy and will improve with experience, Gujarat Titans head coach Ashish Nehra said on Monday.Gill took over as Gujarat Titans captain after Hardik Pandya left the franchise. He led the team to the IPL final in 2026, after Pandya and Nehra had guided GT to the title in their first season in 2022 and another final in 2023.Nehra said Gill and Pandya are very different personalities and leaders, but both have the ability to keep learning."They are very, very different. You are talking about north pole and south pole. Both of them were like me, not somebody who has done much coaching," Nehra said, comparing Pandya and Gill."Both of them were not somebody who has done much captaincy, but you learn on your way forward, and suddenly somebody is pretty much doing captaincy for India in two formats. He is only going to get better."'Gill observes more and to the point'Nehra said Pandya was very open with him and trusted him completely during their successful partnership at Gujarat Titans.Gill, on the other hand, is quieter and more reserved but remains eager to learn."One thing is for sure: he (Pandya) completely trusted me, which was the perfect, perfect thing. He will always be keen to learn. He will always ask if something doesn't go right or doesn't go well. He is somebody you can have lots of conversations with," Nehra said."The other way around, Shubman is a little reserved, a little shy, but that's okay. Everyone is different. There is no right or wrong. He (Gill) is someone who will not talk or have as many conversations as Hardik Pandya, but he is to the point. He is somebody who is very keen to learn and keen to observe. Of course, he is a work in progress. He is only 26-27, and it is not that he has been doing captaincy for so many years. It is only 1-2 seasons, and you learn things and you will get better," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan Cricket Board investigating 'discipline and conduct' of team in latest twist on crisis tour of England
articles.summary: Pakistan dropped seven players from their touring squad after being heavily beaten by England in the first two Tests; watch the third Test between England and Pakistan, at Edgbaston, live on Sky Sports from Wednesday, September 9
articles.body:
Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's to fall 2-0 down in the three-match series.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston, which begins on Wednesday.

A statement read: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.

"The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.

"At this stage, any speculative reports or unverified claims circulating on certain platforms, particularly those originating from hostile external sources, should not be regarded as credible."

The banished senior players included Salman Ali Agha - who captained Pakistan in the first Test before being dropped for the second - wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, who did not bat in either innings after suffering a low-grade calf strain in the field.

Former captain Shahid Afridi described the PCB's decision to make sweeping alterations to the travelling party as the "most shocking decision ever by a selection committee".

Of the seven replacements who have been called up, only batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have Test experience.

The PCB's statement on Monday added: "The PCB will not comment further at this time. The board advises stakeholders and the public to rely on official PCB communications."

New Pakistan coaches in the dark over investigation

Noffke addressed the media in Birmingham on Monday, admitting he was unaware of the specifics of the probe.

"I can be really honest in that I don't know too much," he said. "I sit outside of that decision-making model, (which is) above us as coaches. We try and keep the players focused on what they need to worry about.

"One thing that I've learned about being in Pakistan and coaching for a period of time, nearly 15 months now with the white-ball team, is there's always something going on in the background.

"I think most of the time it's out of the players' control. They need to focus on the cricket that they have in front of them and the opportunity they have in front of them.

"We're not really in the position to even know the outer workings of what's happening at PCB in that context."

Noffke also admitted that taking over mid-series as part of head coach Hesson's staff was "unusual".

He added: "It doesn't happen very often and I guess from Mike and my perspective is all we can do is come in and add positivity.

"We want to listen to the players as much as we can, so there's obviously a feeling of uncertainty but also they've just got back on the job."
